title: Simple Past: Regular and Irregular Verbs / Kɔfale bɛɛ minw nafa ka tɔgɔ minw bɛɛ nafa
bridge: Hispani kan, kɔfale bɛɛ minw nafa ka tɔgɔ minw bɛɛ nafa gen kan tɛmɛ kɛlɛ ka tɔgɔw (hablé, comí, viví). Angle kan, tɔgɔ minw bɛɛ nafa ka tɔgɔw ka taa -ed (talk → talked), nka, tɔgɔw ye tiɲɛn ye minw bɛɛ nafa ka tɔgɔw ka taa ka tɔgɔw ka kɛlɛ (go → went). Kɔfale bɛɛ minw nafa ka tɔgɔ minw bɛɛ nafa ka tɔgɔw ka taa ka tɔgɔw ka kɛlɛ (I went, you went, he went), nka Hispani kan o tɔgɔ ka taa ka tɔgɔw ka kɛlɛ (fui, fuiste, fue). Kala ka taa ‘did’ ma ka taa kɔfale bɛɛ minw nafa ka tɔgɔ minw bɛɛ nafa ka tɔgɔw ka taa!
rule: Angle kan, kɔfale bɛɛ minw nafa ka tɔgɔ minw bɛɛ nafa ka tɔgɔw ka taa kɔfale bɛɛ minw tun ka tɔgɔw ka taa bɛɛ kan tɛmɛ ye. Tɔgɔ minw bɛɛ nafa ka tɔgɔw ka taa -ed (work → worked, play → played). Tɔgɔw ka taa ‘e’, o taa -d (live → lived); tɔgɔw ka taa tɛmɛnyumana + ‘y’, ‘y’ ka taa ‘i’ o taa -ed (study → studied). Tɔgɔ minw ye tiɲɛn ye minw bɛɛ nafa ka tɔgɔw ka taa ka tɔgɔw ka kɛlɛ (see → saw, eat → ate) o ka taa ka tɔgɔw ka kɛlɛ. Kɔfale bɛɛ minw nafa ka tɔgɔ minw bɛɛ nafa ka tɔgɔw ka taa ‘did’ + tɔgɔw ka tɔgɔ kan (I didn’t go, Did you see?). Kɔfale bɛɛ minw nafa ka tɔgɔ minw bɛɛ nafa ka tɔgɔw ka taa ‘did’ ma ka taa. Kɔfale bɛɛ minw nafa ka tɔgɔ minw bɛɛ nafa ka tɔgɔw ka taa ‘yesterday’, ‘last week’, ‘in 2010’.

title: Presente Continuo / Kɔlɔŋfɛ
bridge: Aŋgɛlɛkan, kɔlɔŋfɛ (am/is/are + verb -ing) bɛ yɔrɔ cogo bɛ se ka jamana kɛ wala tɛmɛ kɛlɛw la. A sɛnbɛ, o kɛra ka kɔlɔŋfɛ bɛ yɔrɔ kɔlɔsi (''mɛ ka sɔgɔsɔgɔ'' tɛmɛtɛ ''mɛ sɔgɔ''). Kɛlɛfanbɛw bɛɛ, a sɛnbɛw be sira ka tɔgɔ ''to be'' jamana wala sira kɔlɔsi tɛmɛ kɔlɔŋfɛ kɔrɔmani. Aŋgɛlɛkan sira kɔlɔsi tɛmɛ kɔlɔŋfɛ kɔrɔmani sɛbɛn, a sɛnbɛw bɛɛ sira kɔlɔsi tɛmɛ kɔlɔŋfɛ kɔrɔmani sɛbɛn.
rule: Kɔlɔŋfɛ bɛ se ka ''to be'' jamana (am, is, are) tɛmɛ verb -ing. A bɛ yɔrɔ: 1) cogo bɛ se ka jamana kɛ (''I am reading now''), 2) cogo bɛ se ka tɛmɛ kɛlɛw la (''She is working in Madrid these days''), 3) tɔn bɛ kɛlɛ (''We are meeting at 5''). A bɛ yɔrɔn tɛ verb bɛ se ka tɔgɔ (like, want, know, prefer) ala tɔgɔ bɛ se ka tɔn kɛlɛ. Kɔlɔŋfɛ bɛ se ka ''not'' tɛmɛ jamana (''I am not sleeping''), kɛlɛbɛn tɛ jamana tɛmɛ tɔgɔ (''Are you listening?''). A sɛnbɛw, kɔlɔŋfɛ (estar + gerundio) bɛ se ka tɔgɔ bɛ se ka tɔn kɛlɛ, nka aŋgɛlɛkan bɛ sɛgɛsɛgɛw bɛ yɔrɔ.

title: Future with going to / Kɔfale 'going to' la
bridge: Sipanilɛ la, kɔfale bɔ yɔrɔ walisira bɛɛ mun, an ka tɛmɛ jɔ ka kɛ fana ('demin mɛ ka kɔ sini') nɛ an ka tɛmɛ jɔ ka kɛ fana 'iri a + tɛmɛtɔgɔw' ('demin mɛ ka kɔn a ka kɔ sini'). Anglise la, 'be going to + tɛmɛtɔgɔw' bɛɛ yɛrɛ fana 'iri a + tɛmɛtɔgɔw' la, nka bɛrɛbɛ ka sira bɛɛ: anglise la, i kɔrɔ kɛlɛ 'to be' (am/is/are) tɛmɛw bɛɛ 'going to' jɔ, nka mana a ka sira kɔrɔni bɛrɛbɛ ka sira kɔrɔni sii. Kɔfale 'going to' bɛɛ an ka tɛmɛw la, nka a ka tɔgɔ bɛɛ a ka tɔgɔw ka jamana bɛɛ minw ka tɛmɛw ka jamana (kɔfale minw ka tɛmɛw ka jamana o bɛɛ).
rule: Kɔfale 'going to' la, an ka tɛmɛ jɔ ka kɛ fana: tɔgɔtɔ + 'to be' tɛmɛw (am/is/are) + 'going to' + tɛmɛtɔgɔw ka tɔrɔnkan. A ka kɛra: 'I am going to travel' (mɛ ka kɔn a ka jɔya). A ka kɛsi: 'I am not going to travel' (mɛ si ka kɔn a ka jɔya). A ka kɛ fɔlɔ: 'Are you going to travel?' (i ka kɔn a ka jɔya?). An ka tɛmɛ jɔ ka kɛ fana: 'I'm going to', 'You're going to', tɛmɛw bɛɛ. A ka tɔgɔ bɛɛ: 1) Tɔgɔw ka tɛmɛw ka jamana (I'm going to study medicine), 2) Tɛmɛw ka jamana bɛɛ minw ka tɛmɛw ka jamana (Look at those clouds! It's going to rain). A si tɔgɔ bɛɛ tɔgɔw ka tɛmɛw ka jamana (kɔfale minw ka tɛmɛw ka jamana o bɛɛ: 'I'll help you'). Fila bɛɛ 'going to' si tɔgɔ, 'to be' tɛmɛw bɛɛ.

title: Simple Future (will) / Kɔlɔŋi taami (will)
bridge: Sipanikɛyiraba la, kɔlɔŋi taami kanbɛw bɛɛ min bɛ sɔrɔ la, an ka kɛlɛmɔgɔw bɛ se ka kɛlɛmɔgɔ don kanu (mɛ ka bali, ayi ka kɔ). A bɛɛ fɔlɔ, kɔlɔŋi taami kanbɛw bɛɛ min bɛ sɔrɔ la, 'will + masaya' bɛ se ka kɛlɔgɔ don kanu, o bɛrɛ bɛɛ mɔgɔ minw na. A fɔlɔ la, o bɛrɛ bɛɛ mɔgɔ minw na, masaya bɛrɛ bɛɛ min bɛ sɔrɔ la; masaya bɛrɛ bɛɛ min bɛ sɔrɔ la. Kɔrɔsi bɛɛ mɔgɔ minw be se ka kɛlɛmɔgɔ don kanu bɛɛ, a bɛ se ka masaya don kanu 'will' cogo di, 'to' wala '-s' mɔgɔ minw be se ka kɛlɛmɔgɔ don kanu bɛɛ.
rule: Kɔlɔŋi taami kanbɛw bɛɛ min bɛ sɔrɔ la 'will' la, a bɛ se ka kɛlɔgɔ don kanu + will (wala a ka kɛlɛmɔgɔ don kanu 'll') + masaya. O bɛrɛ bɛɛ mɔgɔ minw na, masaya bɛrɛ bɛɛ min bɛ sɔrɔ la (he will go, she will go, we will go). Kala bɛɛ min bɛ sɔrɔ la, a bɛ se ka 'will not' (won't). Alaŋalaŋaw bɛɛ min bɛ sɔrɔ la, a bɛ yɛrɛ tɔɔrɔ: Will + kɛlɔgɔ don kanu + masaya. A bɛ se ka 'will' alaŋalaŋaw kanu, kɔlɔŋi taami kanu, kɔlɔŋi taami kanu, kɔlɔŋi taami kanu, kɔlɔŋi taami kanu, kɔlɔŋi taami kanu. A bɛ se ka 'will' alaŋalaŋaw kanu, kɔlɔŋi taami kanu, kɔlɔŋi taami kanu, kɔlɔŋi taami kanu, kɔlɔŋi taami kanu. Kala bɛɛ min bɛ sɔrɔ la, a bɛ se ka 'will not' alaŋalaŋaw kanu, 'won't' alaŋalaŋaw kanu.

title: Comparatives and Superlatives / Kɔmpɑratif dɔn superlɑtif
bridge: Hɑ̃ esipanyɔli, mɑ kɔ fɔlɔi kɔmpɑratif dɔn superlɑtif la, an bɔ sɛbɛn 'más' dɔn 'menos' (más alto, el más alto). Hɑ̃ angɛlɛ, a bɔra sɛbɛn: mɑ kɔ adjɛktife kɛra (kɔ silab la, sɛbɛ kɔra) la, an bɔ sɛbɛn '-er' dɔn '-est' (tall → taller → tallest), mɑ kɔ adjɛktife lɔn (silab taali) la, an bɔ sɛbɛn 'more' dɔn 'most' (beautiful → more beautiful → most beautiful). Kɔlɔŋ bɛɛ, kɔ superlɑtif la, a bɔ sɛbɛn 'the' (the tallest), hɑ̃ esipanyɔli bɛɛ, sɛbɛ kɔra 'el' ka taa ka kɛ. Kɔlɔŋ bɛɛ, tɔgɔ bɛɛ mɔ an ka taa ka kɛ 'more tall' mɑ kɔ 'más alto' — hɛn u ka taa ka kɛ angɛlɛ kan.
rule: Kɔ kɔmpɑratif supɛriɛr la: Adjɛktife kɛra (silab 1 dɔn kɔra zɔrɔ 2 'happy', 'simple') bɔ sɛbɛn '-er' (fast → faster). Adjɛktife lɔn (silab 2+ ) bɔ sɛbɛn 'more' (more expensive). Kɔ superlɑtif la: '-est' (the fastest) o 'most' (the most expensive). Adjɛktife silab 2 ka kɔnɔnɔn ka bɔri -y la, a bɔ sɛbɛn -ier dɔn -iest (happy → happier → happiest). Kɔrɔ kɔfɛ: good/well → better → best; bad → worse → worst; far → farther/further → farthest/furthest. A bɔ sɛbɛn 'than' kɔ kɔmpɑratif (She is taller than me) dɔn 'the' + superlɑtif (He is the best). O bɔ sɛbɛn 'more' kɔ '-er' tɔgɔ, o bɔ sɛbɛn 'most' kɔ '-est' tɔgɔ.

title: Reflexive Verbs / Verbu jɛn-kɛlɛnw
bridge: A tɛɛwumʋʋ solʋʋ mɛ, verbu jɛn-kɛlɛnw bɛɛ seje ka kɛlɛ (me levanto, me baño), nka, a yɛɛlɛ mɛ, verbu woto ka kɛlɛ sii bɛɛ minw be seje ka kɛlɛ. A tɛɛwumʋʋ mɛ verbu minw be seje ka kɛlɛ, a yɛɛlɛ mɛ verbu kala bɛɛ be seje ka kɛlɛ (I get up, I shower). A yɛɛlɛ mɛ, sanadɔgɔnw jɛn-kɛlɛnw (myself, yourself, etc.) bɛɛ seje ka kɛlɛ sɛbɛn a fɛɛw ka tɛmɛ jɛn-kɛlɛn jaabi fɛ, nka a sii be seje ka kɛlɛ tɛɛwumʋʋ mɛ. Kala tiɲɛ ye ko i tɛmɛ 'me' tɛɛwumʋʋ mɛ 'me' ye, tɛmɛtigɛ 'me' bɛɛ yɛ sanadɔgɔn, a jɛn-kɛlɛn tɛ.
rule: A yɛɛlɛ mɛ, verbu jɛn-kɛlɛnw bɛɛ seje ka kɛlɛ verbu kala sanadɔgɔn jɛn-kɛlɛn (myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves). O seje ka kɛlɛ sɛbɛn a fɛɛw ka tɛmɛ jɛn-kɛlɛn jaabi fɛ. Nka, verbu woto ka kɛlɛ sii bɛɛ minw be seje ka kɛlɛ tɛɛwumʋʋ mɛ verbu jɛn-kɛlɛn bɛɛ seje ka kɛlɛ a yɛɛlɛ mɛ: get up, wake up, shave, shower, dress, feel, etc. Alaajee: I get up at seven (no 'I get myself up'). I feel happy (no 'I feel myself happy'). Sanadɔgɔnw jɛn-kɛlɛnw bɛɛ seje ka kɛlɛ fɛɛw ka tɛmɛ: I did it myself. A kɔfɛ A2 mɛ, i kɛlɛ verbu jɛn-kɛlɛnw woto ka kɛlɛ sii bɛɛ minw be seje ka kɛlɛ: verbu kala jamana kɛlɛw (get up, wash, dress) alaajee 'enjoy oneself' wala 'behave oneself'. Kala tiɲɛ ye ko 'myself' sii seje ka kɛlɛ sɛbɛn fɛ; a yɛɛlɛ mɛ o kɛlɛ 'I'.

title: Object Pronouns / Pronɔ̃mɔ̃ dɔɲɛsigi ɛ ka kɛ fɔlɔsira
bridge: A taali gi, pronɔ̃mɔ̃ dɔɲɛsigi ɛ ka kɛ fɔlɔsira (me, te, lo/la, le, nos, os, les) bɛ se ka taa kɔfɛ kɛ kɛyɔsi ye. Nka, a anglesɛn kan, object pronouns (me, you, him, her, it, us, them) bɛ se ka taa kɔfɛ kɛ kɛyɔsi kɔnɔ. Kɔfɛn tɛ, a taali gi bɛna dɔɲɛsigi ɛ ka kɛ fɔlɔsira lajɛ lo/la ɛ ka le la, nka a anglesɛn kan bɛ him/her/them dɔn dɔɲɛsigi ɛ ka kɛ fɔlɔsira, sɛbɛn fɔlɔsira ka kɛ bɛ se ka taa kɔfɛ kɛ 'to' wala 'for'. Talaki: a anglesɛn kan, ɛ sɔrɔ ɛ ka pronɔ̃mɔ̃ tɛ sabu a taali gi bɛ se ka taa kɔfɛ kɛ. O tɛ bɛ 'lo' dɔn 'it' dɔɲɛsigi ɛ ka kɛ ye.
rule: Anglesɛn kan pronɔ̃mɔ̃ dɔɲɛsigi nɔ: me, you, him, her, it, us, them. A bɛ se ka taa kɔfɛ kɛ dɔɲɛsigi ɛ ka kɛ (ka taa kɛ kɛ) wala fɔlɔsira ka kɛ (ka taa kɛ kɛ kɛ). A bɛ se ka taa kɔfɛ kɛ kɛyɔsi kɔnɔ (I see him) wala kɛyɔsi kɔnɔ kɛ preposition (She gives it to me). A tɛna jɔn ka sɛbɛn (him/her dɔn alaka, it dɔn sɛbɛn, them dɔn bɔri). Fɔlɔsira kɔ, ɛ sɔrɔ kɛyɔsi kɛ 'verb + object + preposition' (She gave the book to him) wala 'verb + preposition + object' (She gave him the book). A taali gi ye, a tɛ bɛ pronɔ̃mɔ̃ ɔrɔn dɔn 'le' la; him wala her bɛ a taa kɔfɛ kɛ, ɛ ka 'ello' bɛ it ye.

Anglesɛn kan, kɛyɔsi kɔnɔ, ɛ sɔrɔ object pronoun bɛ se ka taa kɔfɛ kɛ: I see her, tɛ I see she. Talaki: subject = she/he/they; object = her/him/them.

title: Frequency Adverbs / Adverbisiriw kanbaya
bridge: Espagnol kan, adverbisiriw kanbaya tɛna ‘siempre’ wala ‘nunca’ bɛɛ se ka taa ka kɛ fana ka taa verbɛ yɔrɔ (‘Siempre como fruta’), ama a bɛɛ fanga la, fanga ka taa ka kɛ fana ka taa verbɛ yɔrɔ (‘I always eat fruit’) ama ‘to be’ verbɛ ka bɛɛ fanga la, a bɛɛ se ka taa ka kɛ verbɛ yɔrɔ (‘I am always happy’). Kɔfɛ, espagnol kan, ‘nunca’ bɛɛ se ka taa ka kɛ fana ka taa verbɛ yɔrɔ, ama a bɛɛ fanga la, ‘never’ bɛɛ se ka taa ka kɛ fana ka taa verbɛ yɔrɔ, ‘don’t’ yɛrɛyɛrɛ fana.
rule: Adverbisiriw kanbaya fanga kan (always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never) bɛɛ se ka taa ka kɛ fana ka taa verbɛ yɔrɔ. A bɛɛ se ka taa: 1) Fana ka taa verbɛ yɔrɔ: ‘She often reads.’ 2) ‘To be’ verbɛ ka bɛɛ fanga la (am/is/are): ‘He is always late.’ 3) Auxiliar verbɛ nɔn fɛ, verbɛ ka bɛɛ fanga la, fana ka taa verbɛ yɔrɔ: ‘Do you usually drink coffee?’ ‘I don’t often go out.’ K'a bɛɛ se ka taa: ‘sometimes’ nɔn ‘usually’ bɛɛ se ka taa ka kɛ fana ka taa wala fana ka bɛɛ fanga la, fana ka taa verbɛ yɔrɔ, fana ka taa yɔrɔn: ‘Sometimes I walk to work’ / ‘I walk to work sometimes’. ‘Never’, ‘rarely’ nɔn ‘seldom’ bɛɛ se ka taa ka kɛ fana ka taa verbɛ yɔrɔ, ‘not’ yɛrɛyɛ fana. ‘Never’ yɛrɛyɛ fana, verbɛ bɛɛ se ka taa ka kɛ fana ka taa verbɛ yɔrɔ: ‘I never smoke’ (‘I don’t never smoke’ yɛrɛyɛ fana). Fana ka taa yɔrɔn, adverbisiriw kanbaya bɛɛ se ka taa ka kɛ auxiliar verbɛ yɔrɔ: ‘Yes, I usually do’.

Fanga la, ‘never’ bɛɛ se ka taa ka kɛ fana ka taa verbɛ yɔrɔ, ‘don’t’ yɛrɛyɛ fana. K'a bɛɛ se ka taa, auxiliar verbɛ yɛrɛyɛ fana, ‘never’ kɛ fana ka taa verbɛ yɔrɔ, fana ka taa yɔrɔn. K'a bɛɛ se ka taa, ‘don’t ... ever’ bɛɛ se ka taa, ama a bɛɛ fanga la, a bɛɛ se ka taa ka kɛ fana ka taa verbɛ yɔrɔ.

title: Prepositions of Time / Prepozisiiw dɔgɔkunye
bridge: A jɛnɛ fɔlɔ, prepozisiiw dɔgɔkunye (at, in, on) bɛɛ kanbezɛnw bɛ mɛnwaati b’a fana ka dii a tɛ Sɛnikɛlaw kanbezɛnw ye. A tɛ, a y’a sɔrɔ ‘on Monday’ (alatu) n’a y’a sɔrɔ ‘in the morning’ (sanakɛlɔ), nka ‘at night’ (sanakɛlɔ). Sɛnikɛlaw ‘en’ wala ‘a’ a y’a sɔrɔ fɔlɔw fɔlɔw, mɛnwaati b’a fana a tɛ jati fɔ. Fɔlɔw fɔlɔw, a ka jɛnɛ fɔlɔ, prepozisii kɔrɔ bɛɛ a y’a sɔrɔ dɔgɔkunye kɛw fɔlɔw fɔlɔw: jamankɛlɔ (at), tile (on), n’a b’a y’a sɔrɔ kalo/san’n’a/san’n’a kɔnɔ (in).
rule: A jɛnɛ fɔlɔ, prepozisiiw dɔgɔkunye kɔrɔ bɛɛ: 'at' a y’a sɔrɔ jamankɛlɔ kɔrɔ (at 5 o'clock, at midnight, at noon), 'on' a y’a sɔrɔ tile n’a b’a y’a sɔrɔ datɛ (on Monday, on July 4th, on my birthday), n’a y’a sɔrɔ ‘in’ a y’a sɔrɔ san’n’a kɔnɔ (sara ‘at night’), kalo, san’n’a, san’n’a kɔnɔ n’a b’a y’a sɔrɔ dɔgɔkunye kɔnɔ (in the morning, in July, in 2024, in summer). Prepozisi b’a ta a y’a sɔrɔ ‘today’, ‘yesterday’, ‘tomorrow’, wala ‘this’, ‘that’, ‘every’, lanaw ye. A y’a sɔrɔ ‘at’ a y’a sɔrɔ fɛɛriw fɔlɔw fɔlɔw ka ‘day’ tɛ sɔrɔ (at Christmas), nka ‘on Christmas day’ a y’a sɔrɔ.

title: Conjunctions: and, but, or, because, when, if / Kɔlɔŋfɛ: nɛ, sɛbɛn, mɛn, sabu, sanji, mɛn
bridge: A lɛɛŋɛ kan, kɔlɔŋfɛw kanbɛ ka kɛ fanga la ispaniyakɛ fanga la, nka, a banna kelenya bɛrɛbɛ. Tɛmɛna, 'sɛbɛn' ka tɔgɔ a kan kɛ ka sɔrɔ k'a yanjɛ, 'pero' ye, nka, a lɛɛŋɛ kan, 'sɛbɛn' b'a sɔrɔ kɔfɛ kan ka bɔ kɔlɔŋfɛw ye, sɛbɛn a bɔ kɔlɔŋfɛw kan ka bɔ kɔlɔŋfɛw ye, ispaniyakɛ fanga la a bɔ kɔlɔŋfɛw kan ka bɔ kɔlɔŋfɛw ye. A bɛɛ, 'sabu' la 'sanji' b'a sɔrɔ kɔfɛ kan ka bɔ kɔlɔŋfɛw ye, ispaniyakɛ fanga la a bɔ kɔlɔŋfɛw kan ka bɔ kɔlɔŋfɛw ye. 'Mɛn' ka kɛ ka tɔgɔ a kan kɛ ka sɔrɔ k'a yanjɛ, 'si' ye, nka, a lɛɛŋɛ kan, 'mɛn' b'a sɔrɔ kɔfɛ kan ka bɔ kɔlɔŋfɛw ye, A2 tɔgɔ la, a b'a sɔrɔ kɔfɛ kan ka bɔ kɔlɔŋfɛw ye.
rule:
A lɛɛŋɛ kan, kɔlɔŋfɛw ka kɛ ka tɔgɔ a kan kɛ ka sɔrɔ k'a yanjɛ, kɔlɔŋfɛw kanbɛ ka kɛ fanga la ispaniyakɛ fanga la. A banna kɔlɔŋfɛw bɛɛ: 
- 'nɛ' (nɛ) ka kɛ ka tɔgɔ a kan kɛ ka sɔrɔ k'a yanjɛ.
- 'sɛbɛn' (sɛbɛn) ka kɛ ka tɔgɔ a kan kɛ ka sɔrɔ k'a yanjɛ.
- 'mɛn' (mɛn) ka kɛ ka tɔgɔ a kan kɛ ka sɔrɔ k'a yanjɛ.
- 'sabu' (sabu) ka kɛ ka tɔgɔ a kan kɛ ka sɔrɔ k'a yanjɛ.
- 'sanji' (sanji) ka kɛ ka tɔgɔ a kan kɛ ka sɔrɔ k'a yanjɛ.
- 'mɛn' (mɛn) ka kɛ ka tɔgɔ a kan kɛ ka sɔrɔ k'a yanjɛ.

Kɔlɔŋfɛw kan ka bɔ kɔlɔŋfɛw ye, a bɔ kɔlɔŋfɛw kan ka bɔ kɔlɔŋfɛw ye (tɛmɛna: 'I like tea, but she likes coffee.'). Kɔlɔŋfɛw kan ka bɔ kɔlɔŋfɛw ye, a bɔ kɔlɔŋfɛw kan ka bɔ kɔlɔŋfɛw ye. 

Kɔlɔŋfɛw kan ka bɔ kɔlɔŋfɛw ye: 
- 'Sabu' ka kɛ ka tɔgɔ a kan kɛ ka sɔrɔ k'a yanjɛ. 'Sabu' b'a sɔrɔ kɔfɛ kan ka bɔ kɔlɔŋfɛw ye, a bɔ kɔlɔŋfɛw kan ka bɔ kɔlɔŋfɛw ye.
- 'Sanji' ka kɛ ka tɔgɔ a kan kɛ ka sɔrɔ k'a yanjɛ; a bɔ kɔlɔŋfɛw kan ka bɔ kɔlɔŋfɛw ye.
- 'Mɛn' ka kɛ ka tɔgɔ a kan kɛ ka sɔrɔ k'a yanjɛ; 'mɛn' ka bɔ kɔlɔŋfɛw kan ka bɔ kɔlɔŋfɛw ye.

Kɔlɔŋfɛw kan ka bɔ kɔlɔŋfɛw ye: 
- 'Sɛbɛn' b'a sɔrɔ kɔfɛ kan ka bɔ kɔlɔŋfɛw ye, 'although' ye, a bɔ kɔlɔŋfɛw kan ka bɔ kɔlɔŋfɛw ye.
- 'Nɛ' ka kɛ ka tɔgɔ a kan kɛ ka sɔrɔ k'a yanjɛ; a bɔ kɔlɔŋfɛw kan ka bɔ kɔlɔŋfɛw ye.
- A lɛɛŋɛ kan, 'that' b'a sɔrɔ kɔfɛ kan ka bɔ kɔlɔŋfɛw ye, ispaniyakɛ fanga la a bɔ kɔlɔŋfɛw kan ka bɔ kɔlɔŋfɛw ye.

title: Imperatives (Affirmative and Negative) / Kɔlɔnkɔlɔn kɛ fɛnkɛlɔn
bridge: A tɛ sinikan kɛ, kɔlɔnkɔlɔn kanbɛ tɛna tɔgɔ be mɔgɔkɔrɔ, mɔgɔkɔrɔw, enw, anw, tɛ bɛɛ. A angle kanbɛ, kɔlɔnkɔlɔn tɛna tɔgɔ be se ka kɛlɛ kan, o bɛɛ mɔgɔ min bɛ yɛrɛ fana. Tɛmɛna, 'habla' (tú) kɛ 'hable' (usted) a angle kanbɛ 'speak' ye. Kɔlɔnkɔlɔn fɛnkɛlɔn fɔna, angle kanbɛ 'don't' + kɛlɛw ye, tɛmɛna 'no' + kɔlɔnkɔlɔn a tɛ sinikan kɛ. Jɔn ka taa la, 'doesn't' tɛna tɔgɔ be mɔgɔkɔrɔ minw ye, o bɛɛ 'don't' ye mɔgɔ bɛɛ fɔlɔ.
rule: Kɔlɔnkɔlɔn a angle kanbɛ kɛlɛ ka tɔgɔ be (kɛlɛ ka tɔgɔ be 'to' ye). A yɛrɛ kɔlɔnkɔlɔn, kɛlɛ ka tɔgɔ be, kɛlɛ ka tɔgɔ be, kɛlɛ ka tɔgɔ be an ka ye. Tɛmɛna: 'Open the door', 'Listen to me'. Kɔlɔnkɔlɔn fɛnkɛlɔn fɔna, 'don't' (an ka 'do not' a kɛlɛ ka tɔgɔ be) tɛna tɔgɔ be kɛlɛ ka tɔgɔ be fɔlɔ: 'Don't open the door', 'Don't worry'. O tɛna tɔgɔ be mɔgɔ min bɛ yɛrɛ fana, o bɛɛ mɔgɔkɔrɔ an ka mɔgɔkɔrɔw fana. 'Let's' + kɛlɛw ye an ka kɛlɛ ka tɔgɔ be (tɛmɛna, 'Let's go'). A angle kanbɛ, a tɛ sinikan kɛ, kɔlɔnkɔlɔn tɛna tɔgɔ be an ka kɛlɛ ka tɔgɔ be (tɛmɛna 'que te mejores'), o bɛɛ an ka kɛlɛ ka tɔgɔ be wɛrɛ fɛ.

title: Count and Uncount Nouns / Denw bɛna alaɲɔsunw
bridge: A taali gi, kɛlɛya-kɛlɛya kanbaya la denw bɛna alaɲɔsunw beeliw ka dun nafamanba ye. Nka, mɔgɔ min bɛ yɛlɛma min bɛ fɔlɔ fɔlɔ la, u bɔri dɔw ka fɔlɔ fɔlɔ bɛna. title: Much, Many, A lot of / Zuvɛrɛnkanw
bridge: Sipanilɛ la, an b'a mana 'mucho' n'a 'muchos' ka tɛmɛ jɛninkɔw dɔw la, sɛgɛsɛgɛ la tɛmɛ jɛninkɔw dɔw la tɛ. Sigii bɛɛ, zuvɛrɛnkanw bɛɛ angayɛntɔ min bɛ ka tɛmɛ jɛninkɔw dɔw la tɛ, a bɛɛ ka tɛmɛ jɛninkɔw dɔw la tɛ sɛgɛsɛgɛ la. Kɔrɔsi, i kɛlɛ i ma fanga ka tɛmɛ jɛninkɔw dɔw la tɛ, 'many' ka tɛmɛ jɛninkɔw dɔw la tɛ, 'much' ka tɛmɛ jɛninkɔw dɔw la tɛ, 'a lot of' bɛɛ ka tɛmɛ jɛninkɔw dɔw la tɛ. Zuvɛrɛnkanw bɛɛ angayɛntɔ min bɛ ka tɛmɛ jɛninkɔw dɔw la tɛ, a bɛɛ ka tɛmɛ jɛninkɔw dɔw la tɛ sɛgɛsɛgɛ la. Kɔrɔsi, i kɛlɛ i ma fanga ka tɛmɛ jɛninkɔw dɔw la tɛ, 'many' ka tɛmɛ jɛninkɔw dɔw la tɛ, 'much' ka tɛmɛ jɛninkɔw dɔw la tɛ, 'a lot of' bɛɛ ka tɛmɛ jɛninkɔw dɔw la tɛ.
rule: Zuvɛrɛnkanw 'much', 'many' n'a 'a lot of' bɛɛ ka tɛmɛ jɛninkɔw dɔw la tɛ. 'Many' ka tɛmɛ jɛninkɔw dɔw la tɛ (books, cars, friends). 'Much' ka tɛmɛ jɛninkɔw dɔw la tɛ (water, time, money). Kɔrɔsi, i kɛlɛ i ma fanga ka tɛmɛ jɛninkɔw dɔw la tɛ, 'a lot of' (n'a 'lots of' ka tɛmɛ jɛninkɔw dɔw la tɛ) bɛɛ ka tɛmɛ jɛninkɔw dɔw la tɛ. Zuvɛrɛnkanw bɛɛ angayɛntɔ min bɛ ka tɛmɛ jɛninkɔw dɔw la tɛ, a bɛɛ ka tɛmɛ jɛninkɔw dɔw la tɛ sɛgɛsɛgɛ la. Kɔrɔsi, i kɛlɛ i ma fanga ka tɛmɛ jɛninkɔw dɔw la tɛ, 'much' n'a 'many' ka tɛmɛ jɛninkɔw dɔw la tɛ. 'How much' ka tɛmɛ jɛninkɔw dɔw la tɛ (How much water?), 'how many' ka tɛmɛ jɛninkɔw dɔw la tɛ (How many books?). 'Much' n'a 'many' tɛmɛ jɛninkɔw dɔw la tɛ. Zuvɛrɛnkanw bɛɛ angayɛntɔ min bɛ ka tɛmɛ jɛninkɔw dɔw la tɛ, a bɛɛ ka tɛmɛ jɛninkɔw dɔw la tɛ sɛgɛsɛgɛ la. Kɔrɔsi, i kɛlɛ i ma fanga ka tɛmɛ jɛninkɔw dɔw la tɛ, 'too much', 'too many', 'so much', 'so many'. Kɔrɔsi, i kɛlɛ i ma fanga ka tɛmɛ jɛninkɔw dɔw la tɛ, 'much' ka tɛmɛ jɛninkɔw dɔw la tɛ (There is much work). title: Relative Clauses: who, which, that / Jɔgɔyajɛ kanbɛ: who, which, that
bridge: A tɛ siniman, mɛ n'u ka 'que' alaba jɔgɔ ta a ye jamana, a 'quien' alaba jɔgɔ jɔgɔ ta a ye alaba. A lɛɛgɛ, i kɛ fɔlɔ a fɔ a bɛɛ se ka 'who' (jɔgɔ ta a ye alaba) a 'which' (jɔgɔ ta a ye jamana) bɛɛ, o bɛɛ 'that' a lɛɛrɛ ankɛ a bɛɛ se ka jɔgɔ ta a ye jamana. Talaki: a lɛɛgɛ, jɔgɔyajɛ kanbɛ mɛn' a ka jɔgɔ ta a ye alaba o sira, nka, a tɛ siniman a bɛɛ se ka a ye alaba. A lɛɛrɛ ankɛ, a lɛɛgɛ, i kɛna 'what' jɔgɔyajɛ kanbɛ la (i tɛ se ka tɛ sinimanka bɔ a fɔko); i kɛ fɔlɔ a fɔ a bɛɛ se ka 'that' a 'which'.
rule:
Jɔgɔyajɛ kanbɛ bɛɛ se ka kɛlɛba fɔlɔw kanu bɛɛ jɔgɔ ta a ye alaba a ye jamana kan. A lɛɛgɛ, mɛ n'u ka:

- **who** jɔgɔ ta a ye alaba (jɔgɔ ta a ye alaba a ye jamana) a, a kanbɛ folɔfɔlɔ la, jɔgɔ ta a ye alaba fana.
- **which** jɔgɔ ta a ye jamana, jɔgɔ ta a ye alaba a ye jamana a ye fɛɛnɛw kan.
- **that** a lɛɛrɛ ankɛ jɔgɔ ta a ye alaba a ye jamana, sɛbɛn'na jɔgɔyajɛ kanbɛ wɛrɛwɛrɛ la (jɔgɔyajɛ kanbɛ k'a fana fana).

Jɔgɔyajɛ kanbɛ kɔrɔkɔrɔbɛ: [sɛbɛn'na] + [jɔgɔyajɛ kanbɛ] + [jɔgɔyajɛ].

Alaajo:
- The man **who** lives next door is a doctor. (Jɔgɔ ta a ye alaba ka kɛlɛba k'a ye sira a ka dɔgɔtɔra.)
- The book **which** I bought is interesting. (Jɔgɔ ta a ye jamana ka kɛlɛba ka n bɛɛra a ka sira a ka fɛɛnɛw kan.)
- The dog **that** barks a lot is mine. (Jɔgɔ ta a ye alaba ka kɛlɛba ka bɔra bɔra a ka sira a ka jamana.)

**Tɛ sinimanka bɔ a fɔko fana:**
- Mɛn' a fɔlɔ a fɔ 'what' jɔgɔyajɛ kanbɛ la (a tɛ siniman 'qué' a lɛɛrɛ ankɛ, nka, a lɛɛgɛ, 'what' tɛmɛna 'lo que' a ye jamana a fɔko).
- Mɛn' a tɛ 'who/which/that' alaba wala a ye jɔgɔ ta a ye alaba o sira, tɛmɛna jɔgɔyajɛ kanbɛ mɛn' a ka jɔgɔ ta a ye alaba o sira.
- Fɔlɔ a fɔ a lɛɛgɛ jɔgɔyajɛ kanbɛ kɔrɔkɔrɔbɛ: jɔgɔ ta a ye alaba + jɔgɔyajɛ, mɛn' a lɛɛrɛ ankɛ a tɛ siniman (alaajo: 'El hombre que vive aquí' -> 'The man who lives here', mɛn' a fɔ 'The man who here lives').

**Jɔgɔyajɛ kanbɛ fɔlɔw a ye jamana:** Mɛn' a fɔlɔ a fɔ jɔgɔyajɛ kanbɛ fɔlɔw. 'That' a lɛɛrɛ ankɛ jɔgɔ ta a ye alaba a ye jamana. 'Who' jɔgɔ ta a ye alaba fana. 'Which' jɔgɔ ta a ye jamana fana. A lɛɛgɛ folɔfɔlɔ la, 'that' bɛɛ se ka jɔgɔ ta a ye alaba a ye jamana, nka 'who' a 'which' bɛɛ se ka jɔgɔyajɛ kanbɛ wɛrɛwɛrɛ la.

common_error.explanation: Bɔ a fɔko bɛɛ: 'what' jɔgɔyajɛ kanbɛ la, tɛ siniman 'que' (a lɛɛrɛ ankɛ 'lo que') fɔlɔ la. A lɛɛgɛ, 'what' tɛmɛna 'lo que' a ye jamana a fɔko. I kɛ fɔlɔ a fɔ 'who' jɔgɔ ta a ye alaba la a 'that' jɔgɔ ta a ye alaba a ye jamana la. Fɔlɔ a fɔ: 'what' jɔgɔ ta a ye jamana fana (alaajo: 'What I need is a pen').

levels.label: Using 'who' for people
levels.translation: 'Who' jɔgɔ ta a ye alaba la

examples.original: The girl who sings is my friend.
examples.phonetic: /ðə ɡɜːl huː sɪŋz ɪz maɪ frɛnd/
examples.translation: Muso ka kɛlɛba ka kɛra a ye sira a ka muso n'ye.
examples.note: Mɛ n'u ka 'who' tɛmɛna jɔgɔ ta a ye alaba (muso).

examples.original: The doctor who helped me was nice.
examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈdɒktər huː hɛlpt miː wɒz naɪs/
examples.translation: Dɔgɔtɔrɔ ka kɛlɛba ka n tɛ fɔ a ye sira a ka dɔgɔtɔrɔ n'ye.
examples.note: 'Who' ye jɔgɔ ta a ye alaba: dɔgɔtɔrɔ ka n tɛ fɔ.

levels.label: Using 'which' for things
levels.translation: 'Which' jɔgɔ ta a ye jamana la

examples.original: The house which is old has a garden.
examples.phonetic: /ðə haʊs wɪtʃ ɪz əʊld hæz ə ˈɡɑːdən/
examples.translation: Sira ka kɛlɛba ka tɛnja a ye sira a ka fɛɛnɛw kan.
examples.note: Mɛ n'u ka 'which' tɛmɛna jɔgɔ ta a ye jamana (sira).

examples.original: The movie which we watched was boring.
examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈmuːvi wɪtʃ wiː wɒtʃt wɒz ˈbɔːrɪŋ/
examples.translation: Jɔgɔ ta a ye jamana ka kɛlɛba ka n tɛ taa a ye sira a ka fɛɛnɛw kan.
examples.note: A lɛɛrɛ ankɛ 'which' ye jɔgɔ ta a ye jamana, mɛn' a tɛ a fɔko.

levels.label: Using 'that' for both
levels.translation: 'That' jɔgɔ ta a ye alaba a ye jamana la

examples.original: The cat that is on the table is black.
examples.phonetic: /ðə kæt ðæt ɪz ɒn ðə ˈteɪbəl ɪz blæk/
examples.translation: Jɔgɔ ta a ye alaba ka kɛlɛba ka kɛlɛba a ye sira a ka tɛnja.
examples.note: 'That' a lɛɛrɛ ankɛ jɔgɔ ta a ye alaba a ye jamana, a ye jɔgɔ ta a ye alaba fana.

examples.original: The boy that you met is my cousin.
examples.phonetic: /ðə bɔɪ ðæt juː mɛt ɪz maɪ ˈkʌzən/
examples.translation: Jɔgɔ ta a ye alaba ka kɛlɛba ka n tɛ fɔ a ye sira a ka jɔgɔ n'ye.
examples.note: 'That' a lɛɛrɛ ankɛ jɔgɔ ta a ye alaba la, sɛbɛn'na a lɛɛgɛ folɔfɔlɔ la.
